counterfactual_missing_items: No posterosuperior calcaneal prominence or retrocalcaneal bursitis to support Haglund syndrome
No plantar fascia thickening to support plantar fasciitis or plantar fascial fibromatosis
No fracture, lesion, or arthritis to suggest another calcaneal process
decisive_items: pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot showed no thickening of the plantar fascia
no signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow
response.rationale: R2 directly matches the MRI-defining pedunculated bony protrusion at the plantar calcaneal enthesis, consistent with a plantar calcaneal enthesophyte. R5 mislocates the finding as Haglund syndrome, which would involve the posterosuperior calcaneus rather than the posterolateral plantar aspect. R4 and R3 are contradicted by the explicit absence of plantar fascia thickening on MRI. R6 describes an associated examination finding but not the imaging-based diagnosis.

rejected.why: MRI explicitly shows no thickening of the plantar fascia, directly contradicting plantar fasciitis.
No plantar fascia thickening or fibromatosis mass is present on MRI.
Gastrocnemius tightness is a contributing examination finding, not the most likely diagnosis given the bony protrusion.
